Why this exists

How does AI “know” what to write? Tools like ChatGPT and Claude generate text one word at a time, predicting what's likely to come next based on patterns learned from enormous amounts of writing.

Bi-grams and Markov chains are a radically simplified version of that same idea: count how often one word follows another in a body of text, then use those odds to predict what comes next.

Real AI language models are far more complicated than this — they weigh thousands of words of context, not just one, and learn abstract patterns rather than raw counts. But this tool gives you a hands-on sense of what might be happening “under the hood.”

A hands-on tool for text prediction

The Bi-gram Chain

If you had the whole works of Jane Austen, could you auto-generate sentences that sound “plausibly” like her writing?

This app takes in the works of an author and creates a Bi-gram table that shows all the words in the text, and shows what word is most likely to appear next.
